refusal (none)
note No wedge-foot length is stated on the wire or its array or in the assembly rules (none resolve: name a .wasm with the .wBond's AssemblyRef or the workspace's DefaultAssemblyRef), so the built-in starting value 2·d = 50.8 µm was used. It is a first guess, not assembly data: set DefaultFootLengthNm in the .wasm (or FootLengthNm on the array or the wire).
note 2 wedge end(s) were moved in z, by at most 1.18237 µm, so each foot lies on its pad: a foot's axis is its pad's top plus half the section's height. The wires' plan geometry and the rest of their loops are as the .wBond states.
note Port 1 ('1') at (-550, 0 µm) was taken to be on the conductor's low-x (left) end (the port's own direction), driving current in the +x direction, at 50 Ω.
note Port 2 ('2') at (550, 0 µm) was taken to be on the conductor's high-x (right) end (the port's own direction), driving current in the −x direction, at 50 Ω.
note 2 conductor piece(s) are thinner than 3 skin depths at 40 GHz and than 0.1 of their own width, so they are sheets carrying their conductivity and thickness rather than meshed volumes. Both thresholds are provisional.
note 'Pads' names no material, so its σ is a number of unknown temperature and is used as given at 20 °C. Name a material with an α₂₀ to have it evaluated at the operating temperature.
note The air box's floor is 'Ground' as a PEC plane at 0 µm: it is the lowest ground-reference conductor, nothing is drawn on it and nothing is drawn below it.
